answer: Spectral graph partition barriers, arising from eigenvector components of the graph Laplacian, inherently define regions of weak connectivity, preventing global trust diffusion. Personalized EigenTrust attenuates adversarial influence by biasing trust propagation towards known good nodes, causing adversarial weight to rapidly decay across these spectral cuts. This creates an effective isolation reef, ensuring malicious actors within a dense sub-graph cannot spiral their undue influence out like a vast nebula across the honest network.
